briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan's Enforcement Streak Continues as Hemp and Psychedelics Policy Shift Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan's Cannabis Regulatory Agency has kept up a run of multimillion-dollar enforcement actions this fall — closing a processor, revoking a grower's licenses over fake flower, fining a retailer over influencer deals, and a court finding a farm illegally filled protected wetlands. Nationally, Congress bought the hemp industry more time before a THC ban takes effect, a DEA judge kept cannabis rescheduling on hold pending a new GAO report, and the FDA held its first public hearing on the future of psychedelic therapy.

local.text: Michigan revokes 20 grower licenses over fake flower — The Cannabis Regulatory Agency pulled 20 Class C licenses from GP Holdings LLC (dba Millie Montana Industries) of Clare and fined it $2 million after packages labeled marijuana flower tested as dirt and mulch with no THC.

State finalizes $251,250 fine over influencer vape cartridges — The CRA issued a final order revoking the retail license of Budbridge LLC (dba Muha Meds Ypsilanti) for seven rule violations, including illegally handing out vape cartridges to social media influencers.

CRA shuts down processor, levies $2 million fine — Following a contested hearing, the agency revoked Michigan Investment 10 LLC's medical processor license and closed its adult-use processor operation after finding egregious violations of state processing rules.

Fawn River recalls dab product over banned chemical — The company voluntarily recalled its Hash Melts (Green Crack 1G Live Rosin Dab), produced June 16, 2026, after state testing found a banned chemical in the product.

Court finds marijuana farm illegally filled protected wetlands — A 30th Circuit Court judge ruled Bliss Corporate, Inc. cleared, dredged and filled 15.9 acres of wetlands in Sherman Township to build a cannabis farm, with penalties to be decided next month.

national.text: DEA judge pauses cannabis rescheduling proceeding — Chief Administrative Law Judge Derek Julius stayed the Schedule I-to-III rescheduling case so a new GAO report on DEA and FDA's abuse-potential review process can be considered, with responses to the underlying motion due Oct. 13.

Congress delays federal hemp-THC ban to December — A short-term government funding bill signed in early September pushed back the effective date of the 2025 ban on intoxicating hemp-derived THC products, giving the hemp industry three more months to lobby for changes before a 0.4mg-per-container THC cap takes hold.

FDA holds first public hearing on psychedelic therapy — The agency's four-hour hearing on the future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs drew more than 1,800 registered attendees; the FDA said it wasn't soliciting views on specific drug applications or rescheduling, and its public comment docket closed Oct. 5.

Tilray posts record quarterly revenue — The company reported first-quarter fiscal-2027 net revenue of $257 million, up 23% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to about 30% and its beverage unit, including BrewDog, turning profitable.

New York tops $4 billion in lifetime legal cannabis sales — State regulators disclosed licensed dispensaries generated $512.6 million in third-quarter 2026 sales, pushing year-to-date sales to $1.41 billion and lifetime adult-use sales past $4 billion since 2022.
